title: Defender for Endpoint: Advanced Features, Rules and Custom Data Collection

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)
Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint advanced features; configure rules settings in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint; configure custom data collection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Advanced features

Path: Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features. Set a feature On or Off, then Save preferences. The exam picks the feature that fits a stated need.

Advanced feature What it does
Enable EDR in block mode Blocks malicious artifacts even when Defender Antivirus is in passive mode
Automatically resolve alerts Resolves alerts with no threats or remediated threats; does not overwrite alerts you set to In progress or Resolved
Configure allow or block file settings Lets you allow or block files with indicators; needs Defender Antivirus active and cloud-delivered protection
Configure custom network indicators Allow or block IPs, URLs and domains; needs Windows 10 1709 or later, or Windows 11
Enable tamper protection Stops attackers from turning off security features
Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups Stops incident merging across device groups; affects future correlations only
Enable live response and live response for servers Allows live response sessions (Module 13)
Allow unsigned script execution in live response Lets unsigned PowerShell scripts run in a session
Configure automatic attack disruption Turns on automatic attack disruption (Module 4)
Exam tip

. EDR in block mode = Defender Antivirus is passive (for example a third-party antivirus is primary). Allow or block file = indicators and needs active antivirus and cloud protection.

2More advanced features to recognize

Advanced feature What it does
Hide potential duplicate device records On by default; tenant-wide
Download quarantined files On by default; needed to download a quarantined file
Configure web content filtering Needs a web content filtering policy
Enable user details display Shows Microsoft Entra user details in the alert queue and device page
Enable the unified audit log Writes Defender activity to the unified audit log
Enable device discovery Finds unmanaged devices on the network
Share endpoint alerts with Microsoft Compliance Center Feeds Purview solutions such as insider risk
Configure the Microsoft Intune connection Must be turned on in both Intune and Defender for Endpoint
Configure Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps integration Connects endpoint signals to Cloud Apps
Enable authenticated telemetry and Enable preview features Authenticated sensor data; early access to new features
Configure Endpoint Attack Notifications Direct notifications from Microsoft Threat Experts

3Indicators

Indicators let you allow, audit, warn or block an entity. They are managed under the Rules area of Settings > Endpoints.

Indicator type Actions available
Files Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution, Block and remediate
IP addresses Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution
URLs and domains Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution
Certificates Allow, Block and remediate

Limit: 15,000 indicators per tenant; it cannot be increased. The old action alert only is now Audit; alert and block is now Block and remediate.

When several controls apply, the order is: application control (WDAC, AppLocker), then Defender Antivirus exclusions, then block or warn file indicators, then SmartScreen, then allow file indicators, then ASR, controlled folder access and antivirus.

Exam tip

. Certificates have only two actions: Allow and Block and remediate. Files have five.

4Other rules under Settings, Endpoints

Rule type Purpose
Alert suppression Hides alerts that match a rule (Module 1)
Indicators Allow, audit, warn or block files, IPs, URLs and certificates
Custom data collection Collects extra telemetry into Sentinel (next section)
Isolation exclusions, automation uploads and automation folder exclusions Exceptions for device isolation and for automated investigation file handling

5Custom data collection

Custom data collection collects extra endpoint telemetry beyond the defaults and sends it to Microsoft Sentinel for hunting. A rule filters on folder paths, process names or network connections.

Step Detail
Open Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Custom Data Collection
First Select the Sentinel workspace (top right), even if it is already connected
Wizard General Information, Create rule (table, action, conditions), Define rule scope, Review and finish, Submit
Scope All applicable client devices, or devices with dynamic tags
Manage Edit, Enable checkbox, Delete (permanent; history stays in Sentinel)

Data lands in five tables: DeviceCustomProcessEvents, DeviceCustomImageLoadEvents, DeviceCustomFileEvents, DeviceCustomNetworkEvents and DeviceCustomScriptEvents.

Prerequisite or limit Fact
License Defender for Endpoint Plan 2
Sentinel One workspace per tenant
Tags Dynamic tags only (manual tags are not supported), set in Asset Rule Management and run at least once
Clients Windows 10 or 11 at the minimum client version; Windows Server 2019 or later
Volume cap 75,000 events per device per rule per 24-hour rolling window; collection for that rule then stops until the window resets
Delay Deployment typically takes 20 minutes to 1 hour
Exam tip

. Custom data collection needs Plan 2, a Sentinel workspace and dynamic tags. The 75,000 events per device per rule per day cap is the likely numeric question.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company uses a third-party antivirus as primary, so Defender Antivirus runs in passive mode. The SOC still wants malicious artifacts blocked after a breach. Which advanced feature should be enabled?

  • AEnable EDR in block mode for all onboarded devices
  • BEnable tamper protection for all onboarded devices
  • CConfigure web content filtering for all device groups
  • DHide potential duplicate device records in the tenant
Show the answer

Answer: A. EDR in block mode blocks malicious artifacts even when Defender Antivirus is passive.

S2An engineer creates a file indicator to block a hash, but the block never takes effect. Which two conditions must be met for the feature to work?

  • ADefender Antivirus is active and cloud-delivered protection is on
  • BDefender Antivirus is passive and live response is turned on
  • CTamper protection is off and preview features are turned on
  • DDevice discovery is on and the Intune connection is turned off for the tenant
Show the answer

Answer: A. Allow or block file settings need active antivirus and cloud-delivered protection.

S3A SOC needs an indicator type that offers only the actions Allow and Block and remediate. Which type is it?

  • ACertificates, which offer only two possible actions
  • BIP addresses, which also offer Audit and Warn actions
  • CFiles, which also offer five different response actions
  • DURLs and domains, which also offer Audit and Warn
Show the answer

Answer: A. Certificate indicators support only Allow and Block and remediate.

S4A threat hunter needs extra file events from a specific folder on Windows 11 clients, stored in Sentinel. Which table receives the data from a custom data collection rule?

  • ADeviceFileEvents, the default endpoint file table
  • BDeviceEvents, which holds miscellaneous device events
  • CDeviceCustomFileEvents, one of five custom tables
  • DCommonSecurityLog, the table for CEF data sources
Show the answer

Answer: C. File-based rules write to DeviceCustomFileEvents.

S5A custom data collection rule stops sending events from one busy server before the end of the day. What is the most likely reason?

  • AThe rule needs manual tags instead of dynamic tags to run
  • BThe workspace is limited to one custom table per tenant
  • CThe rule reached its cap of 75,000 events per device in 24 hours
  • DThe deployment takes 24 hours and has not finished yet
Show the answer

Answer: C. The cap is 75,000 events per device per rule per 24-hour rolling window.

S6A company with two device groups does not want incidents to combine devices from different groups. Which advanced feature meets the requirement?

  • AAutomatically resolve alerts for every device group
  • BRestrict correlation to within scoped device groups
  • CEnable unified audit log for every device group
  • DConfigure automatic attack disruption for the tenant
Show the answer

Answer: B. The feature stops incident merging across device groups for future correlations.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Where are the advanced features of Defender for Endpoint configured?

Show the answer

Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features.

R2What is the maximum number of indicators per tenant?

Show the answer

15,000.

R3Which two actions does a certificate indicator support?

Show the answer

Allow and Block and remediate.

R4Which license does custom data collection need?

Show the answer

Defender for Endpoint Plan 2.

R5What is the new name of the old "alert only" indicator action?

Show the answer

Audit.

R6Which tables receive custom data collection events?

Show the answer

DeviceCustomProcessEvents, ImageLoadEvents, FileEvents, NetworkEvents and ScriptEvents.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Advanced features Settings > Endpoints > General > Advanced features
Passive antivirus EDR in block mode
Allow or block files active antivirus and cloud-delivered protection
Indicators files 5 actions, IPs and URLs 4, certificates 2; 15,000 per tenant
Custom data collection Plan 2, Sentinel workspace, dynamic tags, five Device Custom tables
Cap 75,000 events per device per rule per 24 hours
